lesson.title: React useEffect Hook Introduction
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Set up React counter component
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React project (npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react), run npm install and npm run dev, and render MyComponent in src/App.jsx. In src/MyComponent.jsx, import useState and useEffect, add a count state starting at 0, and render a paragraph plus an Add button wired to addCount.

targets.caption: Declare the count state variable and addCount updater

explanations.topic: What useEffect does and its three trigger modes

hints: Did you create the Vite React app and render <MyComponent /> inside src/App.jsx?
Import both useState and useEffect from "react" at the top of src/MyComponent.jsx.
Use const [count, setCount] = useState(0); and update it with setCount(c => c + 1); inside addCount.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to export default MyComponent or import it into src/App.jsx
Using onClick={addCount()} instead of passing the function reference onClick={addCount}
steps.code:
import React, {useState, useEffect} from "react"; function MyComponent() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); function addCount(){ setCount(c => c + 1); } return (<>

Count: {count}

); } export default MyComponent;

steps.title: Run useEffect on every render
steps.instructions: Inside MyComponent, add a useEffect call with an arrow function and no dependency array. In the callback, set document.title to a template string showing the current count.

targets.caption: Set document.title inside useEffect without a dependency array

explanations.topic: Running useEffect after every re-render when no dependencies array is passed
Empty dependency array runs side code only once on mount

hints: Where should useEffect be placed inside a function component?
Place useEffect(() => { ... }); near the top of MyComponent, after useState.
Assign document.title = `Count: ${count}`; inside the arrow function.
common_mistakes: Using regular single quotes instead of backticks for the template literal `Count: ${count}`
Calling useEffect inside a nested helper function instead of at the top level of the component

steps.title: Limit useEffect to component mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so the title only updates when the component first mounts. Click Add in the browser to verify the count increments while the page title stays unchanged.

targets.caption: Add an empty dependency array to run the effect only on mount

explanations.topic: Running useEffect on mount plus when a specific dependency changes

hints: What second argument tells useEffect to run only once?
Pass an empty array [] after the callback function in useEffect.
Your call should end with }, []);
common_mistakes: Leaving out the comma between the callback function and the dependency array
Omitting the empty array when you only want one-time initialization on mount

steps.title: Trigger useEffect on count changes
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add count to the useEffect dependency array so the title updates on mount and whenever count changes. Also add a subtractCount function and a Subtract button to test decrementing count.

targets.caption: Include count in the dependency array

explanations.topic: Difference between no dependency array and [value]

hints: Which state variable should trigger the title update?
Put count inside the dependency array: [count].
Duplicate addCount to create subtractCount using setCount(c => c - 1); and wire a Subtract button.
common_mistakes: Putting quotes around "count" in the dependency array instead of passing the state variable
Mutating count directly instead of using setCount(c => c - 1)
steps.code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]); function subtractCount(){ setCount(c => c - 1); } <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>

steps.title: Watch multiple dependencies in useEffect
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add a color state starting at "green", a changeColor function toggling green/red, a Change Color button, and style the paragraph with {{color: color}}. Include ${color} in document.title and use [count, color] as the dependency array.

targets.caption: Re-run the effect when either count or color changes

explanations.topic: Why missing a dependency causes stale title updates
Benefits of useEffect for organization and cleanup

hints: Notice how changing color does not update the title until color is listed as a dependency.
Create color state with useState("green") and toggle it with a ternary in changeColor.
Update the dependency array to [count, color] so either state change updates document.title.
common_mistakes: Using single curly braces style={color: color} instead of double curly braces style={{color: color}} in JSX
Forgetting to add color to the dependency array when color is used inside useEffect
steps.code:
const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`; }, [count, color]); function changeColor(){ setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green"); }

Count: {count}

steps.title: Track window resize with useEffect
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, create width and height state initialized from window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight and render them in two paragraphs. Define handleResize to update both, and register window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array.

targets.caption: Attach the resize event listener once on component mount

explanations.topic: Why adding an event listener outside useEffect leaks listeners on every re-render
Why React Strict Mode runs useEffect twice in development

hints: Initialize width and height with window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight.
Define handleResize to call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
Wrap window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); inside useEffect(() => { ... }, []); so only one listener is added.
common_mistakes: Calling window.addEventListener directly in the component body, causing thousands of duplicate listeners
Forgetting the empty [] dependency array on the listener setup effect
steps.code:
const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth); const [height, setHeight] = useState(window.innerHeight); useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []); function handleResize(){ setWidth(window.innerWidth); setHeight(window.innerHeight); } return (<>

Window Width: {width}px

Window Height: {height}px

);

steps.title: Clean up the resize listener
steps.instructions: Inside the resize useEffect in src/MyComponent.jsx, return a cleanup arrow function that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED".

targets.caption: Return a cleanup function to remove the resize listener on unmount

explanations.topic: When the useEffect cleanup function runs (before re-render or on unmount)
Using multiple useEffect hooks in the same component

hints: How does useEffect know what cleanup code to run when a component unmounts?
Return a function from inside your useEffect callback.
Return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener immediately instead of wrapping it inside a returned arrow function
Passing a different function reference to removeEventListener than the one given to addEventListener
steps.code: return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }

steps.title: Add a second useEffect hook
steps.instructions: Below the first effect in src/MyComponent.jsx, add a second useEffect that sets document.title to `Size: ${width} x ${height}` whenever width or height changes.

targets.caption: Use a separate useEffect hook to sync document.title with width and height

hints: Can a React component call useEffect more than once?
Add a second useEffect call right after the resize listener effect.
Set document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; with [width, height] as the dependency array.
common_mistakes: Putting the title update inside the mount-only [] useEffect instead of creating a new one with [width, height]
Omitting width or height from the second effect dependency array
